Considering the title of Fullon Hotel, the cleanliness level has a lot of room for improvement, especially the toilet and shower room. All the iron parts are rusted or peeled. The carpet in the room is also yellow in some places and black in some places, which looks old and dirty. In short, it feels like staying in a 1800 hotel. (The above is purely personal opinion).

There is only one type of pillow, which is soft and short. It is recommended that the hotel provide other types of pillows for selection. In addition, the mattress is not clean enough. You can clearly see a lot of hair stuck on the mattress under the sheets. However, the hotel provides free bath balls. The service of the early shift staff is better. They carefully understand the needs of the guests and provide assistance.

To be honest, Yuanshan is really worth experiencing, but the facilities of the basic room are too old and feel dirty. If you only talk about the room, it is really not worth the price, but the reputation, hotel environment, and service are all very good. The bathroom leaks seriously, the sheets and pillows have a musty smell, and the mattress is super hard.

The 14th floor city view was great, and the pillow was uncomfortable, but due to the nature of traveling in Taiwan, 
I walked 20,000 steps every day and fell asleep without even realizing that my neck was sore!! 
I used a shower filter, but the filter color didn't change, and the water quality was👍
I stayed for 3 nights, but the cleaning was only to the extent of changing the trash, floor, and towels, so the bathroom wasn't very clean or anything. 
I was worried because there were a few cockroach issues, but I didn't see a single cockroach in the hotel! There were no mosquitoes or flies. 
The bathroom smelled a little, but it was clean and nice😃😃

It is convenient as it takes about 5 minutes from Songjiang Nanjing Station and about 15 minutes to Nakayama. There are many restaurants and convenience stores nearby, so you won't have any problems even with a long stay. Cleaning revealed some dusty areas in various places. My room was on the seventh floor, but there was insufficient water pressure; the faucet had a decent flow, but the shower only dripped a little from the head. Breakfast had several side dishes, but different items were served on consecutive days, so I didn’t get bored.

I was glad that there was someone at the front desk who could speak Japanese. However, although it was old, the smell of mold was quite strong. There was also mold around the air conditioning, which was a bit disappointing.

The toilet was well cleaned and close to Taipei Station, but everything else was bad. The price was not cheap, and the employees responded with a blunt expression until the end, rather than a four-star hotel. The reply mail to the inquiry before the stay was also not systematic and very late. Above all, the smell of mold in the room was too severe and humid. There was no soundproofing at all, so I could hear the sound of talking and showering in the next room. I'll never use this place again.

The hotel is conveniently located just 10 minutes from Ximending. The restaurant on the 12th floor offers a fantastic view of the river. While the hotel's 80s decor has a certain charm that I actually enjoy, the amenities are outdated, poorly maintained, and dirty. For these reasons, I cannot recommend this hotel.

- The room smells like a street toilet
- The sheets were old and dirty, with stains twice in a row
- A musty smell
- Wardrobe doors are dusty to the point of knotting
- Swimming pool far away
There are more and better options in Taiwan for $700 or so
￼￼￼￼The room is clean and comfortable, that is, the billiard room is a bit dirty, can be cleaned clean as well.

Area for bath is very small. 
Bed is not clean, causing many red spots on both legs.

old room with musty odour, poor lighting, poor noise insulation, dusty and old furnitures that has not been wiped down properly, little toiletries provided, stained old carpets 
apathetic service by counter staff and  bellboy
 feels like a motel then a supposedly 5 star hotel

It is old after all. Old grand hotel style.
There was a bathtub but it looked dirty so I never used it even though I stayed for 3 nights. The shower had strong pressure and hot water but the drainage couldn't keep up. There was a smell coming from the drain.
The tap water also smelled, and I brushed my teeth with mineral water. The disposable slippers were nice.
There were no outlets around the bed, which was inconvenient.
There was a safety deposit box.
About a 12-minute walk from Exit 6 of Ximen Station.
20-minute walk to Huaxi Street Tourist Night Market.
The bed and linens were clean.

The cooling water tower in the room is noisy, the sound insulation is poor, the carpet is dirty, the toilet is not clean, there is a lot of dust, and the equipment is old. Suggested rectification and improvement.
The transportation location is good and close to the business district.
Convenient for shopping, eating and drinking.

Although it seems like it's meant to be luxurious, the entire hotel is very dimly lit, including the rooms, lobby, and first-floor service hall. The bathroom isn't clearly separated from the room itself, and the large, round bathtub is separated from the room only by a curtain. The room was very damp, and the quilt smelled musty. The carpet was also extremely dirty, with black stains all over the floor. I tried to wear slippers, but they weren't disposable, but reusable slippers worn by many people. The air conditioner was also quite loud, and the noise, dampness, and musty smell all night long didn't really feel like a five-star hotel. Although it was my first time here, it would also be my last.

There are many better hotels in Taipei. I stayed at this hotel for one night, paying about ¥80,000, but the service was not commensurate with the price. Here are some of the negative aspects:

- The doorman wasn't always present. Even when he was there, he didn't open the door.

This isn't an automatic door, and I was surprised that a luxury hotel doesn't have a doorman.

- The lights in the room were out.

I wonder if they don't check when they make the bed? The room cleaning was also sloppy.

- You can't charge your phone by the bed these days.

This is understandable considering the old facilities, but the power outlets were poorly located.

- The flush in the bathroom was weak.

- The shower room had poor drainage.

- The buffet food was placed in a disorganized manner.

- The cereal was over there, the coffee over there, the omelet over there—it was a complete mess. The food tasted amazing, like a luxury hotel.
Even though we were on a high floor, the windows were dirty and the view was unclear.
This defeats the purpose of choosing a high floor. I hope they clean it up soon. Photos of the Taipei night view and the nearby Taipei 101 all look dusty.

While it's understandable that the facilities are old and shabby, the lack of maintenance and service is stark for a world-class luxury hotel.

I recommend this hotel to people who like old hotels and don't mind spending money.

Initially, they did not give us a room according to the order information. In the end, they asked us to wait an extra 40 minutes before checking in. The problem was that it was already past 15:30. Normally, the room should be tidied up. Then we found a big cockroach in the room at night. Hygiene is very bad
The facility is old and moldy. The lamp stand is rusty and airconditioner is dusty.

On the first day, I found one cockroach, which I got rid of and was able to live normally after that, but on the second day, three appeared, so I had to change rooms. Other than that, the service was polite and the hotel was close to the station, so it was good.

The shower was not powerful enough, the hot water was not hot enough, the hot water from the wash basin was rusty, and the whole T-shirt was stained black and brown. A big hotel should not have any mistakes.

When I checked in, I already knew that it was a renovated old hotel. This time I stayed on the executive floor. The room was large, but it still retained many old equipment. The bathroom was old and not cleaned thoroughly. The restroom in the lobby was very old. I couldn't believe it was a five-star hotel. Five star prices, but not five star quality. Although the hotel has many breakfast options, the cooking skills need to be improved. During the four nights of stay, there was not a single breakfast that could be praised.

I booked it because it was close to Ximen Station, but it's a bit far to call it close. The room is small, so you can only open one suitcase. The bathroom sink has black mold stains on the rim, which makes me feel uncomfortable every time I use it. And the soundproofing isn't great, so the toilet flushing is so loud it wakes me up in my sleep... That's all I'll say.
1st room was horrible, mouldy and dirty, I need to complain about it and they give me an other room in L7, was ok but the neighbours too noisy, I need to call reception around 2 am .

The location is good, the room are spacious, staff is very attentious, but the hotel is old. In the corridors, the wallpapers are peeling of and the carpets look dirty. Everything smell of mould and old cigarrettes.

Considering the value for money, there's nothing I can do about it, but I can't help but feel a little disappointed.
First of all, the power cord is Taiwanese, so it won't plug in to a Korean cord without a power strip.
Even the cord was in a corner, behind a dusty drawer, which was a hassle.
The windows are quite noisy. The wind blowing sounds like a haunted house.
I think it's because the windows are old. There's a whooshing sound.
The lighting is generally dim, and it's a keyless entry, not a card key.
The market isn't close, and the station isn't close either.
I don't think I'll come back.
But if you're looking for value, Notbed is the place to go. It has everything you need.
The room was small and there were no sofas, so I sat outside in the lobby and ate. There seems to be a lobby on every floor, and it's not bad. The sofas are comfortable. The photo shows the radish rice cakes I ate while sitting there.
If you're just going to sleep, I recommend it.

Booked 2 rooms (2 nights) for our family trip and the location of the hotel is perfect. Just across the metro. The rooms were of adequate size but needs improvement though. The carpets were dirty and soiled, the shower head is loose ,some dirty spots around and the pillows were too flat. But the services provided by the staffs were excellent. Provided us with good suggestions on how to go around. Will be return back to the same hotel again on our last part of our trip.
The room is so dirty and dark. Table and chairs like also. Not soundproof. The pillow also dirty 😅
it was perfect except for I saw a huge cockroach in swimming pool loacker room

The carpet in the room is very dirty and can even see the stains. The furnishing are old and I find not very clean. On the first day I felt my body itchy when I slept but was quite alright on  subsequent days. Also the hotel and the room is too dark. The plus point is the good location which is near Taipei train station and the staff are helpful.

Nice maintained but a bit dated. Lack of outlets and I can't find any outlet to accomodate my mac book jumbo plug I end up unplug the standing light near the door.  Service was great otherwise.  Carpet is cream color a bit dirty and have stains.

The bed covers and pillows have obvious stains, the facilities are very old and have many mold spots. I would not recommend it with a score of 10. The only advantage is that it is close to the MRT station.

I stayed for 2 nights. I think the location is convenient as it is just one subway station from Taipei Central Station. The room was newly decorated and clean, and I appreciated that they provided four bottles of water each day. I used the rooftop pool and large public bath. It was unfortunate that the pool was enclosed and hard to see outside. In the large bath, there seems to be a rule that you must wear a shower cap even after washing your hair, and I received guidance from a regular customer about this. The room, like everywhere else, didn’t seem like it had been cleaned much, as the windows were dirty.

The hotel is not luxurious, and the rooms and bathrooms are old. It is not dirty, but it is not as clean as in Japan. However, the overwhelming location is attractive. It is a key transportation point, and there are many restaurants nearby, so it is not inconvenient.

We stayed at this hotel based on our tour guide’s recommendation, as we had missed a night at another hotel. Although advertised as a 4-star hotel, our booking did not include breakfast, so we had to walk out to nearby eateries, which were okay.

The hotel is pretty old, though reasonably maintained. However, the room was dusty upon arrival, which caused some sneezing, and it did not match the published pictures. The hotel is not near Xi Men Ding Night Market, but they do offer a shuttle bus that can be booked to travel to the night market with pick-up at a set time.

Overall, the stay was adequate for a short visit, but guests should not expect a modern 4-star experience or a central location.

The breakfast is OK, the facilities are not worthy of a 5-star hotel, the access card is a key, the carpet is very dirty, the staff is very polite, more than 2,000 a night, it is not comparable to 5-star domestic hotels,

This hotel really needs a good upgrade. The interior furnitures are quite old, you could smell mould once you step into the room. Bad sound proof. The only good thing is it's really close to the Taipei main station, right next to it.

It’s the worst experience ever in my entire having stayed in a hotel as dirty as this one.  The first room I was assigned was dirty with hair on the bed under pillow and desk.  Obviously the room wasn’t cleaned properly.  I reported this to the front desk and then was assigned to another room and the second room is very smelly and humid.  I rejected that second room and they arranged another room, then this third room again had hair on the bed under pillow .  I had no choice but was compelled to take the room instead of continuing changing another room.  The room which I finally stayed is still very dirty everywhere.  There is mold everywhere in the room, on the wall paper, every corner, the ceiling in the bathroom is the worst.  This is awful!  The hotel is old but it doesn’t mean that the places can be dirty.  It’s the worst hotel accommodation  experience ever.  I wouldn’t want to stay in such a place even if this is free of charge.  Having stayed in the hotel brought me a bad memory to my trip.

Dated design, but very good location. 

Staff is good overall. 

Generally clean but found a dead cockroach in the toilet though.

Pros: The hotel is located close to the MRT, within a 5-minute walk. The room is relatively large and 4 bottles of water are provided daily. Ask if you need sanitary products when checking in.
Cons: The room has a sense of age, with chipping in many places and a slight musty smell. The sheets were stained. There was hair in the bathtub and dried boogers on the bathroom wall.

In addition to the convenient location, the facilities are outdated and the rooms are too dark. On the first day, I called to ask for a hairdryer replacement and there was no follow-up until I checked out. After cleaning the room, the slippers were taken away and new ones were not returned. The toilet board is stained again.

The room was dusty because the hotel was vewry old.  Things like amenity,  towel, bed sheets are clean and maintained well but other part is questionable. Suits for group tourist since just near Taipei main station.

When my family arrived, the lobby was super crowded,(maybe due to new year) and a great place to take pictures. 

The room was quite big, but the toilet was quite dirty. The bathtub had brown stains, and the corners of the toilet were caked in mold.

The hotel was connected to Taipei Main Station through Exit M6. There was a lift directly connected to room.

We took a Tra train one stop to Rouhe night market, it was very convenient.

Overall, Caesar Park Hotel Taipei was a nice place to stay in.

First of all, the facility is excellently located next to Q mall with links to Taipei main station.
Secondly the staffs are courteous and accommodating.
Thirdly the dining area for breakfast was large enough and not crowded.
Fourthly chambermaids are courteous and hardworking. Very helpful too.
Cons:- (1) Place a bit dark not bright due to its concept. (2) My wife got bitten by bed bugs (3) l saw a tiny cockroach crawling on the food display table during breakfast. 
Suggestion: Get pest control company to deal with the problems.

Can not think of any good description of this place. Only location is convenient. Lobby, hall way, rooms every where are so dark. Furnitures’ paint are fainted. Carpet looks so dusty and old. Toilet smells, and bathtub is higher then my knee which is so dangerous and difficult to use. Very bad experience.

Thus hotel is situated just beside Taipei Main Station. It's very convenient to go anywhere because the main station is well connected to many MRT lines. 
The only complain is the place is a bit dusty. I would expect the staff to tidy up the place before letting anyone move in. The hotel is also a bit old. Breakfast is just average.

We booked for 3 nights at this hotel ended up booking a different hotel and left straightaway the next day. 

Our room had a private hot spring and the shower was right next to it, the walls and ceiling in that showering room were covered with mold! As the steam goes up during shower it forms drips of water and it falls back on you along with the mold. It disgusting!! And the furnitures in the bedroom all had stains on it. It was very disappointing and unhygienic.

The hotel is quite old but overall are good. Staff is very nice, room is big with bathtub.
But room is quite old and dusty for some area.
Not a 5 star hotel. The room is full of smoke smell. The facilities are old and dirty, sheets are dirty, carpet old and dirty. Swimming pool, sauna and spa were closed.

The bathroom door got stuck and couldn't  be properly closed. And what even disappointing was that we saw a dead cockroach on the floor
When we were about to check out. This is a historical hotel with very friendly staff, but considering to be a five start hotel, it needs innovation.

The hotel is really big and spacious, which I liked, but cleanliness could be improved. There was some dust under the bed, the floor felt a bit oily, and the bathtub looked quite dirty. The place seems pretty old, though it’s still fairly well-maintained overall. However, I don’t think it’s very suitable for families with babies — even the baby cot provided felt quite old and worn out. It’s okay for a short stay if you don’t mind an older-style hotel, but not the best choice if you’re looking for something super clean or baby-friendly.

The location is the best in Taipei Main Station.
Here is Ximen Station Ximending. museum. Shilin Night Market. Carrefour. Central Memorial Hall. Yongsan Temple. Convenient to Sammi Restaurant, etc.
Directly connected to Airport Railroad MRT. City airport check-in available

But you have to give up everything else.
low ceiling. Room humidity is high. A bit cold when the air conditioner is on. A bit difficult to control water
bathtub mold. The smell of the shower curtain. If there is water on the floor, you may fall and break your head while wearing slippers
There is a window, but it is tinted black and it is connected to the roof, so it is very dangerous
I don't like 220 volt irons or dryers. barely working
It's hard to find the way, but if you take the Airport Railroad and go to the M6 from the 1st basement floor, you will be connected to the Hotel Elbe.
Don't get confused!

The hotel is not close to mtr station. It's difficult to find if not familiar to the place. The hygiene condition is a bit poor with stained found in bathroom and desk. The room is not too small with this price and with bathtub at which it's not easy to find in Taiwan.

The location and staff were overall friendly and nice.
Because it's old, it's a little dirty.
If you are not sensitive, you will be satisfied.
Breakfast was just so-so, maybe it wasn't to Jae's taste.
This hotel my family like it is comfortable. Next trip will consider this hotel. Just the mini bar have dusty.

The two-day stay at 228 was a very bad experience. The entire door panel of the bathroom was covered with mold spots that were too scary to look at. When I wanted to watch TV in the room, it was suddenly turned off. Even though I wasted a lot of time to start over, it wouldn't turn on again - ridiculous!
When I went to sleep, I stared at the light at the door of the room and couldn't turn it off, and the noise of the refrigerator motor was heard all night long. It was really too annoying. How could I sleep well?
In addition, the most frightening thing is that there are small cockroaches crawling in the closet.
It is called a 4-star hotel, but it doesn't live up to the reputation...

Hotel is focused on the aesthetics rather than delivering real quality service to improve customer experience. It’s a beautifully constructed and decorated hotel, but perhaps the GM should direct more time to inspecting service quality rather than making the floral arrangements. Don’t understand why housekeeping did not pick up obvious things such as desk phone that’s not working (wire was damaged and hanging loose), pens were all dried up, holder in shower room was loose and the bottles of shampoo n gel came crashing down bruising my feet. Buffet breakfast spread was quite sad and quality wasn’t that great either. I even saw a small cockroach crawling around the raw beef area and had to request before they changed out the food. Some of the staff were smiley and warm, but there were really some odd balls that actually look grouchy, like the night shift front desk manager.
The whole hotel feels like it's full of mold😫😫Service is all about efficiency and indifferent attitude

The location is excellent, right next to Taipei 101. The hotel lobby is elegantly designed, very suitable for taking photos and checking in! 
Facilities: The hotel facilities are a bit old, standard facilities of a star-level hotel. It's quite satisfactory! 
Hygiene: Not clean! The kettle is dusty on the bathroom washbasin mirror. The dust on the ground is not mine!

The housekeeping Staff was rude when asked to change the bed sheets. Actually refused until we insisted. Drinking cups were not clean throughout the 4 days. we had to clean them daily. (coffee and Tea). The location is great, but the staff will require better training and customer service.

The hotel is located near the Taipei Main Station. The corridor connects to the hotel. It is very convenient to travel by skytrain, train, there is a Family Mart next to the hotel. Below and around the hotel there are restaurants, McDonald's, shopping malls near the hotel. The room is okay, but there is a lot of dust, the air conditioner is dirty. Maids clean just enough. Vacuum and clean only the bathroom. Daily towel change, toiletries, drinking water replenished daily. If you want to change pillowcases or bed sheets, you must inform the receptionist. There is a kettle for hot water, tea, coffee, hair dryer drive, safe box, shoes in the room. Bathrobes with shower cream, shampoo for shower zone The TV isn't very clear but it's okay to watch. Wifi is available. There is a Starbucks in the hotel. Luggage can be deposited before check-in time.

The second night we stayed in the main building. Compared to the annex, the inside of the building is beautiful, and when there are few people, I took various pictures in the lobby and stairs. The city view from the window of the room was also very beautiful. The refrigerator in the room had sauce on it and was a little dirty. It would have been better if I could have checked in advance.
Old/Dirty.

Usual 5 star amenities and comfort that one would expect. However some staff at reception here seemed unfriendly , being unhappy to be disturbed from whatever chores they were doing. I also saw a baby cockroach in the bathroom.

I had high hopes for the Santos Hotel to be a great value due do its high Agoda rating, but I was misled (and the ratings are inflated). I've stayed in hundreds of hotels but never had such terribly paper-thin walls and porous doorways...EVERY SINGLE SOUND from surrounding rooms and the hallway sounds like it's on a microphone into your room. It makes one worry about the construction, quite frankly. Since I had very loud partying guests who punctuated the entire early morning with shouting, laughter, etc., I got no sleep my first night there. I reported it 3x and the hotel staff would just call them and ask them to quiet down, with no real repercussions at all. This went on literally all night: 2am, 3am, 4am included. In addition, the upkeep of this property has been extremely poor, as evidenced by falling-apart furniture, damaged fixtures, and worst of all, EXTENSIVE mold throughout the entire bathroom. It's enough to make your skin crawl. This hotel has no business charging more than 500 NT/night, not the 3200+ NT per night that I was charged! It was an absolute ripoff.

Overall, hotel is decent and new. Location is about 7 to 10mins from Ximen station and walking distance to Carrefour.

Cleanliness is average as housekeeping did not clean the hidden corners of the shower. 

Definitely not 5 star service as the hotel called us at 12pm if we are checking out. 

Communication with Front Desk tend to be difficult if you speak English and there is a sense of anxiety whether the hotel understands what a guest needs
It is an old property, dirty, old, smelling, needs a complete renovation. Very disappointed.

Our hotel originally specified a two-bed room, but the hotel refused and was forced to upgrade to a single room (Jack). I was really unhappy about the five-star reputation. We were asked to pay an extra NT$4,000, so we had to accept it happily. Later, We found that the room was very unclean, and the old sewage from the hotel was dripping directly on our heads. We really experienced things that we didn't expect. I don't want to stay again!

Our stay at Check Inn Nanjing (March 2024) was uncomfortable because of the overall poor cleanliness, dim/dark atmosphere, and old/outdated building. We stayed on the top floor in one of the bigger rooms. Here are some things that bothered us (See my Google review for pictures) :
1. The large window inside our bedroom looked like it had old paper towel pieces dried up and stuck on the glass. We asked the front desk to remove the debris and wipe down the window before we left for the day. When we came back at night there was nothing done to the windows by housekeeping even though they made our bed and took out the trash. 
2. Looking further into the windows, we found cracked paint and mold along the window frames. Seemed like the hotel managers/owners didn’t even bother to look into the details of keeping the place maintained. 
3. The overall design the bathtub 🛁 was unsafe. Firstly, the bathtub is elevated and rocked side to side when standing to shower. It was difficult to get in/out of because there’s no grab bars or anything steady to hold. Not even a towel rack nearby so you can grab a towel to dry off. 
4. There’s also no shower curtain to keep water from splashing out which led to puddles on the floor. So the combo of a tall unsteady tub, wet floor, no grab bars, or towel holder nearby made it riskier to slipping/falling when showering. 
5. The washer/ dryer area was not kept clean or well maintained. Washing machine smelled like mildew and dirty water. Lint buildup in the dryer filter created a dusty room. In the morning we requested the staff to clean/wipe down the machine, then came back at night expecting to use it but found there was nothing done. We decided to wash/dry our clothes at a laundromat. 
6. The whole atmosphere was dark/dim from the elevators to the hallways and even inside the rooms. Probably to “hide” the flaws and make the outdated space seem unnoticeable. Overall not a comfortable hotel to stay at.

I was initially allocated a room on the fifth floor. When I opened the closet to hang my coat, a dead cockroach suddenly fell on the floor. After informing the hotel, I changed rooms to the 7th floor. However, I changed to a connecting room. The soundproofing was extremely poor. We chatted in the next room until the evening. It’s almost 12 o’clock, I can hear everything clearly, I can’t sleep at all, the experience is really bad🙃🙃

I purposely went to a hotel with windows, but they made it so you can't open them. The windows were covered in moisture and the glass was dirty, so I couldn't see outside very well. 
The air quality was bad, and the humidity was 90-93%, so everything was damp and damp. 
When I got home, all my clothes smelled moldy. 
It was 18-20 degrees during the day and 16-17 degrees at night, 
but it was so cold at night that I barely slept with two extra blankets. 
The biggest disadvantage was that it was old, especially the windows couldn't be opened, 
and they were so dirty and old. And the humidity was high, 
so the cold air circulated and it smelled moldy. 
The advantage was the perfect location connected to the subway and convenient transportation. 
And there was a bathtub, and the room was somewhat spacious, and the cleanliness was good.

First of all, when you get off the elevator, the smell of sewage fills the air. It's very smelly. I was given a room facing Taipei Station, but it was really dirty. The air conditioner smelled moldy and there was a lot of dust. I was surprised that dust would accumulate on the screen of my cell phone or tablet just by leaving it there for a while. The bathroom was also very moldy, so I didn't feel like taking a bath. There were stains on the towels. I stayed for three nights, but the room wasn't cleaned properly, and paper and other items weren't replenished, so I called the front desk many times.
The front desk staff took too long to check in, and were too sluggish.
Also, when I entered the room, a man suddenly pointed his cell phone camera at me and took a picture of me, which was really scary. I asked the front desk, and they said it was okay because it was a hotel staff member, but it was really scary. I hope they stop doing things like that in the future.
It's just a good location, but I don't want to stay at this hotel again.
Old hotel, the room is dusty, the curtains are not easy to open, you can hear the door closing on the opposite side, the sound insulation is average

The room was quite spacious, but the windows were dirty, and there was no view. The breakfast quality was decent, but breakfast service ended too early, and we were rushed to check out by 11 AM. Overall, the experience was poor. The hotel felt very dated; they still used traditional keys instead of key cards. It desperately needs renovation and an upgrade. The facilities didn't justify the price, which was quite disappointing.

We stayed for 4 nights. Booked this hotel based on reviews on the location.

But I think what we valued was the superb housekeeping! We have sensitive nose and will kept on sneezing in dusty places. The housekeeping tidied and cleaned our room when we were at breakfast everyday. No sneezing or sinus at all throughout our stay. 

Although I didn't book it at the lowest price, it's definitely worth the price still.

Check in is fast. The hotel is in a quiet location, 15 minutes' drive from Taipei Main Station. It's a pity that I couldn't go to the sky bar because I didn't have a reservation. The room is of medium size. The glass outside the hotel is a bit dirty, but the view outside is vast.

[Advantages]
Easy to find as it's in front of a big road.
Convenience store nearby, and Starbucks is across the street.
Amenities are available.
The rooms are spacious, and the bathrooms are also large.
Overall friendly staff.
Felt well soundproofed.

[Disadvantages]
Slightly strong moldy smell.
It's too dark even with all the lights on.
The dehumidifier looks dirty as if it hasn't been cleaned properly.
No heating available; only air conditioning is functioning.
Location is great. Near to taipei mrt and taoyuan line. There was a cockroach in the room. The bed was too firm as well.

😃 This is my first stay at the "Fuhua Hotel" on the 24th floor, where I can enjoy the beautiful view of Kaohsiung and the swimming pool, which is really great! 
The hotel has many facilities, including a children's play area (suitable for children under three years old)! 
The gym 💪 and swimming pool 🏊‍♀️ are open from 7 am 🕖 already 👍 
The pool has an adult area and a children's area, and there is also a small massage warm pool for relaxation 😇, plus staff providing towels! 🫶 
The front desk staff are friendly! 
The room is spacious, and the front desk automatically added a small bed for the child upon check-in 👍, the room is quite clean and the soundproofing is good; it lives up to its five-star rating 💯 
One area that needs improvement is the bathroom, as there are a few black mold spots on the bathroom glass seal... 😟😟 
🥳 The breakfast is very rich 🍌🍉🥗🫙🍜🥚🍞🥬🍠🧀🍚🍨☕🥛.... with plenty of choices, and it tastes pretty good 🫶

I forgot to take pictures of the room. The room was not super clean. One of the lights in the room was broken, but the staff came to change it immediately. The bathroom had a bathtub, but it had a lot of mold stains and was a bit old. Fortunately, the hotel has a hot spring bath.

Stayed for 2 nights. On the second morning, I went out and asked the staff to help me empty the trash can (because the capacity was very small). When I came back in the evening, my bottle of facial cleanser was missing. I searched many places but couldn't find it. Maybe the cleaner accidentally dropped it? You may want to pay attention to it~

Breakfast is buffet style, with plenty of choices so you can eat as much as you want before going out to play.

The hotel has many rooms, the place is clean and the rooms are spacious, but the bathroom facilities are a bit old and the sofa chairs are a bit dirty. It would be even better if some media devices could be added, such as Bluetooth speakers. Overall it's a good hotel.

The lobby is small and simply decorated, but the window is large and faces east, so the room is bright and has a good view. The bathroom design also allows for natural light. There are many reception teams. The hygiene of details, such as the mold around the bathtub, is not handled well. The lobby service is good. There are often doormen to open the car door. There are welcome coffee and bath blind boxes to welcome guests. There is also a bag of candy every day to attract guests, but there is no pillow for sleeping.

Very convenient to move around Taipei and even outside Taipei but the lights are quite challenging to figure out how to turn on & off. Carpet in the hallway made it too difficult to move the luggage, glasses, utensils and sink were not cleaned everyday.

I stayed for three days. The room I stayed in the first day had a foul smell, was old, dirty, and the towel was tattered. The next day I changed the room and it was a little better. But after moving in, I found that there was a problem with the TV safe and I had to ask someone to come and repair it. Unfortunately forgot to take pictures for record. This stay experience was really very bad, dissatisfied.
Very old guest rooms that look nothing like website photos.  Bathrooms have old fashioned small tiles with dirty grout.  Does not measure up to other 4-5 star hotels in Taiwan.

There are no tissue boxes in the bathroom and pantry. There are no children's sandals provided when children are booked. The zinc basin in the pantry was not cleaned one day during the stay. The mineral water provided is not enough. It is not as good as expected or rated on the Internet. The buffet has a variety of desserts, but the rest is really mediocre, including not much seafood and very few side dishes. It's not possible to cook udon with the shrimp or abalone on the side. It's really bad. The price is too expensive, I won't come here again.

I thought the cleanliness of Japanese hotels would be very good. But when I entered the bathroom, I saw that the bathtub was very dusty and there were hairs. The towels were black and stained and there were hairs.
The most shocking thing was that the tableware was very dirty during breakfast. There were no signs of cleaning on the juice cup. I thought there was only one. I picked up the other 4 and looked at them again. They were still very dirty. I was immediately scared and dared not use them.
After communicating with the hotel staff, I thought it would improve the next day. I was still disappointed. The cup was still sticky and had not been cleaned.
Before it was time to enter the room, there was a waiting time for afternoon tea, which was quite nice.
But if I go to Taiwan again, I will definitely not stay at this hotel again.

Very disappointing Taiwan housing trip.

Good location, big enough room, although a bit old, but convenient. There are problems with the room, and we immediately changed the room to improve it. There is mold in the seams of the bathroom tiles, which is not cleaned. I hope it will be better in the future. I will still choose to stay there because the price is cheap and the service staff are great. Thank them for their hard work.

The facilities are old and the hygiene is not good.

The hygiene is really bad
The hotel price is very good. Compared to the quality and nearby areas, but would like to improve the cleanliness a little more because there is hair in the bathroom and the carpet is dusty

The location of the hotel is fantastic, just a few minutes walk to Taipei Station.

The carpet was quite dirty and the decoration of the hotel room was quite old. The toilet is OK.

There was a cockroach in the room!!

I will never never recommend this hotel

The room is so small.
Not that clean but not dirty.

I tried the food up there, but it wasn’t worth the price so I recommend going other places.
Hotel was great but the room carpets were abit stained.

1. The hotel service does not pay attention to the small occupancy of guests. 2. All the wall wallpapers in the room were covered with thick dust. As soon as you entered the room, you could see that there was a strong smell in the room and that it had not been soaked in water or mold.

The last picture is a bed sheet with lots of hair and only a screenshot of part of the video?

Cleaning is not done well. You can still see some small garbage. There is a small yellow stain on the bathtub, which should be cleaned by detergent. The surface of the chair looks quite dirty. The wind of the hair dryer is very weak. It is recommended to replace the hair dryer.

Because the hotel was chosen by my family, this hotel mainly accommodates Koreans, Japanese and foreigners. Maybe my family didn’t know the location of this hotel very well. It was too far from the MRT and not too close to the downtown area, so we mainly took taxis every time we went in and out. In addition, the hotel focuses on environmental protection. There is no bottled water in the room. You have to walk out of the elevator to get water every time, which is very inconvenient. This time I stayed for 3 nights. I felt that the cleaning staff did not clean the room thoroughly. Apart from making the bed and toilet every day, they did not clean anything else. There were tea stains and hair on the bedside table that were not cleaned.

After sleeping there for two nights, I couldn't help it and wrote a note on the bedside table hoping that the pillows could be replaced, but no one paid any attention to it. But overall it's good. The hotel is old and all the furniture is old. Bathtub is also dirty which I don’t even dare to use. Location is not good as it is 15mins walk to Ximen metro station. It is also quite dark at night if you walk back from Ximending.

Booked a room that was supposed to be 33sqm, it definitely wasn't and a large part of the space was the balcony.

The toilet smelt absolutely disgusting, complained the first day and they sent housekeeping. The lady did not take off her shoes before walking into the room and later pretended like there was no smell. Kept telling me it smelt fine, and at one point even suggested that we had already used the toilet hence the smell!!! Deep down they know there's a problem with the piping because the lady came with an air purifier and lemongrass spray. It's obviously a complaint they receive all the time hence she came ready prepared. Complained the second day and they just left the bottle of lemongrass spray in the room.

Room is dated, mouldy and dusty, just look at the photos. Even the bathroom door partially broke off. The only good thing about the hotel is the location. Everything else left very little to be desired

The hotel staff at reception were completely unhelpful and missierble. 
The hotel was run down and dirty.

Never again terrible!!!!
The facilities are old, the toilets are not clean, the garbage (used soap) of the previous guest has not been cleaned at all... The room smells musty, and the windows cannot be opened...

It had been a while since I'd stayed here and I was feeling nostalgic, but then I found a cockroach in my room. It was disappointing.
The breakfast selection was as good as before and delicious.

It was a bit far from the subway station, but not far from Ximending, so it was okay, but maybe because the building was old, the rooms were very old tourist hotel style and smelled like mold. Above all, maybe it's just me, but the air conditioner was turned on in the empty room, so even with the air conditioner turned off, the room was very, very cold.

For one of the best business hotels in Taipei, it fell way short of expectations. The room was not cleaned properly prior to check-in and we found cracked dry noodles on the floor. The hotel can be described in one word: Mold. The smell is terrible. I don't understand how they even got a health certificate. Everything is very old, the water doesn't drain, and you wash in knee-deep water.
Location is good!

The location was very good and the room was nice with a view of Taipei Main Station, but there was some grime on the walls, hair on the cushions, and a dusty smell from the air conditioner that seemed to have not been cleaned for a long time.

The cleanliness of the bathroom was a bit of a concern. Also, the bath towels were dirty. Other than that, I was quite satisfied.
There were staff who could speak Japanese, and it was directly connected to the station, which was great.
It's quite old. The room has an unpleasant smell (like mold).

I asked for a clean room, and the bed was really high-quality and clean. There was no mold on the toilet table. Even the remote control was clean, not to mention the toilet. It was great. It was even more ideal than the last stay~

Wifi was unreliable

Came here for the Edward Yang movie nostalgia as it was a prominent location in his film YiYi. Room was extremely spacious and comfortable. Love the high ceiling. Gym has most stuff you’d need for a quick workout. Swimming pool is proper. However, certain areas aren’t exactly very clean (dead cockroach on the floor at the complex where Family Mart is located.) Location is not exactly convenient, especially in this summer heat, but that’s a given if you’re booking here. All in all, an experience to try once and once only.

We have requested 2 cribs as we travelled with our twins. The location is very good and the staff is kind.  But, I would never stay there again. The first room had a musty carpet smell from the entire floor to the room, so I asked for a room change. The second room had a cockroach in the bathroom, and another in the breakfast restaurant. I wouldn't recommend this hotel unless you can endure cockroaches.
I have stayed many times, and the dirty under the bed is a common problem in most hotels. Already booked again, hope Yuanshan can improve!

The rooms booked for 2,900 on other websites can have hot springs. The location and service are good, but the hotel is really old. On the day my friend checked in, he found that the toilet was not cleaned properly and the room also had a smell. The hotel is old, but at least it needs to be kept clean. If there is a musty smell, it should be dealt with the day before. Although the service staff has a very good attitude, it has caused trouble for the residents to not sleep!

Really regretful accommodation experience!

The room is quite old and the bathroom lighting is too dim.

The ********* staff were generally friendly and the service was good.

Breakfast was disappointing because there wasn't much to eat on the second day. The mall connected to the hotel was different from what I expected, with only familiar ********* brands.
And the prices were a bit high. The small supermarket in the basement was okay for a quick visit.
There's a convenience store and Starbucks next to the hotel, so the location is good, but the facilities are just average for a five-star hotel.

Nice staff all over the hotel, nice room, nice gym/swimming pool, nice restaurant.

Only one thing bothered me - the hygiene standards of the changing/sauna/bath area - the floor of the changing room particularly in the dressing area was full of human hairs!  The big bathing area'stools were covered with mold on the reverse!  Those areas need to be properly cleaned a lot more often. 

Thank you.

Facilities: Many restaurants, swimming pools, parks, and boutique department stores

It's a very old place.

aging of facilities

Connected to mrt via exits M3 and M7. Next to Taipei main station.

Gym available but equipments not working and carpet is dirty.

The room is dirty and my whole body is itchy

Facilities getting old. Windows very dirty. We booked a room with view of 101 Tower, what we see first is the very dirty window.

The service was OK, but the facilities were old and a bit dirty. The room we were given at the beginning had a bad smell, and the room we were given at the beginning was very dark and I suspected something was wrong. Later we were given a better room. But there was still a bit of a strange smell.

Overall a decent hotel in a nice & convenient part of Taipei. 

The two double beds were gigantic so sleep quality was great. 

Breakfast spread was decent - not as wide variety as Lin Hotel in Taichung, but quality was definitely good enough for us to eat there every morning for five days.

We were able to open up our luggages on the bench so that was ok otherwise there was not that much floor space to walk and yet have luggages open. 

I liked it that there was a coin laundromat within 5-7 mins away and a nice neighbourhood with good food, bubble tea and cafe options within 3-5min walk. Not to mention this was within 10-15min walk from Ximending. 

Bath tub drainage area was dirty but bath tub/shower area itself was fine. If this was cleaned up, my rating would have been higher.

All things considered, a pretty good hotel that is well decorated and maintained, both in the room & public areas. 

Havent stayed in enough Taipei hotels to know if we can get better value or larger rooms elsewhere. Hence, we are quite happy with this stay but will try to check out other options when we are next back in Taipei.

It was all good except one critical factor for me. There is a damp smell in the airconditioning. My wife did not have an issue with anything except the mosquito bites from me leaving the window open, Ha ha. Staff were all very polite and helpful.

Staff are polite and very efficient and attentive.

The room is not very big overall

When I checked in on the same day, I first tested whether the facilities in the room were normal. One side of the bedside lamp seemed to have a broken bulb and did not light up. I immediately reported it to the counter. Since it was basically unused, I did not ask the staff to replace it.

For one day stay definitely no problem and the wall are quite dirty. The hotel is time for renovation. The location is supper and very near to Ximending.

It was really good^.^ I was a little worried after reading the reviews, but when I went there, the room was okay and everything was clean and neat ㅎㅎ

I'd go somewhere in the middle!!

Hotel room is pretty dusty, and there is still a worn bathroom slipper and an empty bottle underneath the bed

As this place is closer to nature, mosquitoes may be common so get ready some insects repellent! Good thing is the hotel prepared electronic repellent for all guests, very thoughtful of them.

Well located hotel near subway, bus and bike share stations with a pretty good free breakfast! Not the newest hotel (first I've seen in awhile with a CRT TV) but serviceable and with decent wi-fi. Place is nice and comfortable, a little bit dated and dusty but overall a good place to stay in.

The facilities were old, but it didn't feel dirty. I saw some reviews saying it was humid, but it wasn't exactly fluffy, but it wasn't so damp that it was uncomfortable. Good location but not clean.

Very very old. Carpet was dirty.

BUT THE SLEEP... because of how clean the room was, and how clean the aesthetics of the room was, i had the best sleeps in this hotel.
