Will seriously consider staying here again next time in taipei.
Overall nice stay. But when we approach the hotel staff they are quite impolite to the hotel guests. Feel quite disappointed on this.
The male staff in the front desk is unfriendly and charged my room twice( check in and check out). unclear on the procedures

E**za at the front desk of this hotel was the worst Hyatt staff I've ever met, or any hotel staff I've ever been to. She kept asking me what time I would come, saying the room wouldn't be ready at 3 pm. That was very rude and disgusting.
It's your fault that you can't check in at 3 pm, not my problem that I have to come back late. If you're going to do it that way, change the check-in information to 17:00  instead of 15:00 and provide more accurate information, okay?
The staff at the hotel in Ximen where I stayed before Grand Hyatt Taipei were really smart and friendly, so I had high expectations when I went to the Hyatt, but E**za let me down right from tne start.
The facilities of this hotel are good, but the staff  was subpar.
everything was great except for the morning breakfast crew at the restaurant, was kinda rude and sulky.

Hotel room: The soundproofing was extremely poor; I could hear the faucet next door. The air conditioner was old and noisy.

The hotel was incredibly strange. They would persistently ask if I had any laundry early in the morning (I had already ignored them, but they still used their master card to open the door and ask if I had any laundry. This was very strange. If I hadn't been wearing anything, wouldn't that have bothered me? And it was incredibly rude. Someone inside was already playing music, and they didn't hear my knock. So why did they open the door with their master key? Is that such an emergency? I've never seen such a hotel, and it's still a 5-star hotel. Have they not received any formal training? The staff's attitude was also incredibly disturbing. They didn't apologize and just walked away. I asked her name and said I wanted to complain. She told me, "Why would you give me your name to complain?" I was completely baffled. So, what was the point of even opening the door? The hotel's explanation was that they could still file a complaint even if they hadn't asked if I needed laundry. I was completely baffled and speechless. I've never been to a five-star hotel that insists on charging for a change of clothes upon waking up. It requires personal confirmation in the morning. It was a very poor experience.

The location is over 15 minutes from the MRT station, making it inconvenient for traveling with luggage.

The service fell far short of its star rating. It was my fourth visit to Macau, and I received the worst service ever. From the moment of check-in, I had to deal with an unfriendly staff member. I requested confirmation regarding the inclusion of breakfast, and as far as I remember, I had chosen the option with breakfast included. However, when I requested confirmation again, the manager was called, and their attitude was completely disrespectful. They asked me to personally check where it was indicated that breakfast was included in my reservation, using rude and dismissive English. My mood was already ruined at that moment.

Moreover, I could hear every word spoken by other guests in the adjacent room, and the sound of doors slamming in 3am startled me, making it impossible to get a proper night's sleep. The management skills and soundproofing were far from what you would expect from a 5-star hotel. 

After this experience, I realized that, apart from hotel brands under major companies like Marriott, it's difficult to expect good service in Macau. If the price difference is around 50usd, I recommend staying at the W Hotel, which offers better location and services in various aspects.

It was good because it was easy to get to the subway station, airport, and night market. The room was big and the cleaning staff were all kind and nice. In particular, the tea was so delicious that we ate it every day. However, because of a small scratch, I asked the front desk staff in the morning if they had a bandage and asked for two. When I went out in the afternoon to change it, I asked for two more, but a female staff member wearing glasses didn't know I understood Chinese and asked in Chinese why I asked for two more when I gave her two in the morning. I thought it was too rude of a request, so I went to the convenience store to buy more. Except for this part, I really liked the other staff members, so I plan to use it again next time.

I stayed in Hotel Metropolitan Premier Taipei  during Chinese new year. Most of time I was not in Taiwan, I did know hotels may not provide Toiletries but I don’t know how serious it is. I booked Marriott earlier before booking Hotel Metropolitan Premier Taipei, I received an official email from Marriott and restated the policy to me so that I knew what to expect. However for some personal reason I cancelled the booking in Marriott and rebooked with Hotel Metropolitan Premier Taipei, Hotel Metropolitan Premier Taipei has not sent me anything and has no explanations of if the hotel is going to execute the policy or not. When I checked in, I was told if I need Toiletries, I need to pay extra for that. The Japanese manager just came to explained 
And told me that there was some announcement in agoda. First of all, comparing to what Marriott did which was really professional, what Hotel Metropolitan Premier Taipei did was really bad and lack of explanation of policy. Second of all, the Japanese manager explained to me that no customers had this trouble before ever since the policy was announced. I honestly think this is totally nonsense, the policy just announced and the starting execution time is not even a month, there are international travelers, how do you expect everyone to know about this, not to mention about how bad the communication Hotel Metropolitan Premier Taipei is without sending any messages to customers to notify customers. Another problem about Hotel Metropolitan Premier Taipei was the discount of the bakery. I was told from front desk that if I stay in hotel I should get 15%discount of the bakery, but when I went to buy bread, the lady in the bakery said oh the discount is for customers who stay longer than 7 days!!! This is another unprofessional

•	The hotel showed breakfast included on Agoda, but in reality, it was not provided, so keep that in mind (misleading advertising).
	•	The hotel location is good.
	•	The room is also fine.
	•	The staff are friendly (except for one male receptionist who was a bit rude, talked to guests in a dismissive way, and was not friendly toward children).

Extremely rude wait staff at the lobby lounge bar.  Definitely avoid!

Housekeeping also missed my room twice....

This hotel is located right next to the Taipei main station and that makes life so much easier. There is a direct access to Airport, High speed train and local MRT. Also, Q square mall and Taipei city mall are right next to the hotel. Makes it easier for shoppimg and grabbing food or coffee. Hotel has a unique ambience and very spacious rooms. Food at the hotel is quite nice too. Vegeterian options are available as well. Few things were disappointing too 1. Staff was the biggest disappointment, not attentive, least bothered. We took club room and had to follow up with staff to get the order on dinner table. No attentiom from staff whatsoever. No matter if the order is pending, after 8.30PM staff will get busy with setting up the restaurant for brekfast. They even missed serving us the dessert and fruits platter we ordered. Later called us in the room to check if that can be sent to the room. It was quite disgusting. 2. Restaurant takes last order at 8.30PM for dinner. It was always very hurried because most tours in Taipei finish late by 7.30/8PM and by the time you reach hotel, restaurants are closed. 3. Yet another disappointment with staff, we requested for vegan cake for my Birthday. Staff promised to send it to the room on Birthday but never did. Upon following up, they delivered to the room. By that time we had left for our tour. Quite a hassle to deal with the unprofessional staff.
Again bathroom toilet is way too small … Front desk staff needs improvement … Rude and unprofessional!

The restaurant food is on the pricier side. I’ve stayed at other equivalent star hotels on this trip and ordered the same meal and it was less expensive in Taichung. Also it was quite odd they wouldn’t let me order 2 dishes for 3 people - we just landed from the airport and were not that hungry. In fact they were rude. Might as well just order room service at that point. 

The facilities are top tier. The gym is complete and rare to find one with a smith machine and dumbbells heavier than 40 lbs. the sauna and spa is on the newer end as well. I’ve stayed at a 5 star hotel that was not nearly as good. 

Overall a great value. Room was clean. We had one king and single which fits 3 people. I would recommend.

The location is very convenient. Shandao Temple Station is right at the door. It is basically the center of the subway map and the center of Taipei. It only takes ten minutes to walk to Taipei Main Station.
We took a night flight and arrived at the hotel around 1-2 am. The hotel was basically empty at that time, so the check-in speed was very fast. However, the only drawback was that we were still assigned a tail room (actually, this was already written in the order form). No tail room required)

The room is very clean and the bed is comfortable, but the bed is a bit soft for us and makes us more tired after sleeping for a long time (but this is just a personal preference)
The shower facilities are good and the shower water is sufficient. However, I ran out of shampoo halfway through my stay. I have to report it to the staff before refilling it. Even if they don't check the relevant supplies carefully on weekdays,
But the staff responded well. We live on the 9th floor. Basically, the two housekeeping aunts on the 9th floor are very kind and enthusiastic in their work, and they also clean the room very carefully.
The room is also very quiet. You can basically not hear the noise from the street or the voices in other rooms.

However, I have to deduct some points for the facilities. Basically, the TV in the room is not visible. It was relatively good for the first two days. It only bounced occasionally and the picture was framed. The picture quality was also very poor, but I could still watch (listen to) the program content. Later, I basically couldn't turn it on for two days. When I turned it on, the picture was still, and the sound was still electromagnetic sound, which was a bit scary, so I turned it off directly. For me, hotel TV is very important because I want to see the local program culture and relieve boredom in the room. But this trip was basically unavailable. I didn’t receive any notification when I booked a room in advance, and no one informed me when I got to the front desk to pick up a room. It’s just that the TV boot screen said that signal maintenance would be done on the night of August 26th (it didn’t say that it was broken and couldn’t be seen anymore, it looked like it was a regular maintenance)

The hotel swimming pool is not bad, it is a bit smaller than expected/pictured. During the summer vacation, many families go swimming. Basically, they can only soak in the water. There are only 8 sun loungers. It is first come, first served, otherwise you have to wait for others. You can only use it if you leave. There are not many locker rooms/showers, only 2-3 spaces (still very narrow, and they have to be shared with gym guests. Basically, if you go with friends, you still have to go back to the room and queue up for showers, which is very unfriendly and wet. I still have to turn on the air conditioner and wait slowly)
The sauna warmer can be used even by **. This may be due to ********* culture, which is relatively new to tourists. Maybe no one from the front desk to the club reception told me. I had to walk to the sauna warmer by myself to find out that everyone was ** , even if I just want to use the steam room, I have to **, which makes me feel a bit unfriendly, because I went there after swimming, and I was wearing a swimsuit, and I didn’t have clean clothes to leave in after I took them off (originally, I Just wearing a bathrobe)

For this price, the price/performance ratio is 60 points (out of 100 points). There is no doubt that the location is superior, but this brand has such facilities and quality/service, there is still a gap. Out of 60 points, 30 points are given to the location, 15 points to the cleanliness of the room itself, and 15 points to the two aunts who work enthusiastically. If there is a discount, the price is not bad, and the TV is repaired, I will still consider coming again.

If you want to swim (like us) and use hotel facilities, choose something else. There are many good options at this price.

Staff are rude. Breakfast is bad for International travellers, hardly anything there. Even black tea I had to ask them to heat it up on microwave. When breakfast ends, about 20 staff come and chase you out and clear out everything  with loud noises. Towels smells bad, no common area to even sit down and have drink, overall a very bad stay.

A decently priced hotel, but front desk service was lousy and unprofessional. When I arrived, they couldn’t find my reservation. After they found it, they insisted on me paying once more, even though I had already online! Even after producing proper payment receipts, they still wouldn’t believe me. This is not a nice treatment of customers!

I asked for an upgrade to a better room and made it clear that I am happy for pay the difference. They even didn’t bother getting back to me! 

Upon checkout, I called them to request help with my luggage as I had a lot of bags. They said ok. Nobody arrived. Instead, the front desk lady called me and started shouting at me that I must leave the room! When I tried explaining they never sent help, she wouldn’t even listen!

Located near ximending. Hotel provided shuttle bus to ximending too. Room was big and clean. Hotel guest can collect free candies and snacks from the next door cafe, but the counter staff at the cafe was unfriendly and seems unhappy.

Had a disappointing experience. The first room I was given was old, mouldy, and very damp. The hotel provided a dehumidifier, but it was quite noisy at night.

On top of that, the air-conditioning was barely cold. For the first three nights, I was almost sweating while trying to sleep. It took multiple requests before they finally moved me to another room with better cooling.

What made the experience worse was the attitude of the engineering department staff — they were rude and practically implied that I am the problem. Thankfully, the housekeeping staff and front desk were kind and helpful, which I genuinely appreciate.

Overall, not an experience I would expect from a 5 star hotel. I hope they improve their rooms and staff attitude moving forward.

I am a native English speaker and prior to booking this reservation, I had a lot of trouble understanding what some of the negative reviews were regarding this hotel. For example, many of the reviews which were translated from different languages mentioned unprofessional hotel staff.

The staff are extremely professional and are not rude in any capacity at all. They speak English and while they may have an accent, you can figure out what they’re saying if you listen carefully and you can ask multiple times if you need to. 

As for the facilities, the rooms are very art deco and catered to Japanese tourists. Nice touches include a bidet and an iPad in the room which you can use to customize your hotel experience to your liking.

I originally wanted to relax. But when I entered the room, there was a green cloth next to the bed. They should be using it for cleaning! Isn't the Sheraton Hotel a high-end hotel? Why is cleaning unprofessional?
Later, I was given an apple, a diced orange, and a banana. Do you think I'm a monkey? 🤣🤣🤣
I'm wondering if room cleaning is also done casually?
Location was not too near the station, staff's attitude was rather rude.
Good location but staff were very rude

Everything couldn't be better. But one thing was disappointing. I asked for 4 additional towels, but the staff called back and asked me why. When I told them there was no specific reason, rhey gave me 2 more towels. I think it's very rude to ask the customer why they need extra towels. I've never been asked that question until now.
The hotel is in good location but the staff working at the front desk are really impolite (specially Aoi). Also nobody helps with the luggage. It is not a 5 stars hotel.

If you want to stay at this hotel, you need to be able to tolerate bad attitudes.

I checked in at night, and the receptionist was a man in his 50s or 60s with a constant scowl. He was very rude, acting as if I was the one serving him, and seemed ready to lash out at any moment.

After dropping my luggage in the room, I went to a convenience store. As I passed by the front desk, he didn't greet me (which is fine), but glared at me like **********. I was very polite and couldn't understand why he behaved like that at work.

I thought he was the only one like this, but the next morning, when I went to the front desk to extend my stay (because my flight was canceled due to a typhoon), the receptionist named Ally also had a scowl. My goodness, what kind of terrible hotel is this? I asked him something, and he seemed clueless, so he went to the back to ask someone. His colleague came out to help, but with the same impatient expression and harsh tone.

This is the most unfriendly front desk I've ever encountered. If you enjoy dealing with bad attitudes, feel free to challenge yourself by staying here.

Location was the dream (sheltered nearly all the way to the train station), cleanliness was tolerable, cleaning staff were just wonderful. 

The counter girls though, were extremely rude and completely lacking in service skills. They were inflexible, rude and cold. Pity, because they were bad enough that I can’t give Cosmos 4 stars. You can get better service and a more comfortable stay elsewhere for a comparable price.
The front desk staff seemed a bit unfriendly during our check-in process.

We waited a good 15 minutes at the reception for the staff to find our reservation, only for her to retrieve the booking of someone else. The information of another guest was shared by the hotel staff to me as she simply matched the last name of the reservation to my last name, seemingly unaware that it is common for people to have the same last name. At checkout, staff (another person) did not enquire about our stay nor did she ask if we need to deposit our bags for a short while - she simply took our key and waved us away while continued to be on the phone - that is plain rude. All in all, the hard product is ageing, but still ok overall but the staff’s attitude left a lot to be desired.

The old-fashioned room layout, the curtains are thin and do not block the light, and I wake up in the morning. The cheap lamps, furniture and sofas are not comfortable and have no texture.
The swimming pool on the mezzanine is small and low, has no sense of service, is extremely unfriendly, and rushes away from get off work.
The fish for breakfast was not fresh, so I spit it out after taking a bite.
Never lived in such a five-star hotel, very disappointed!

hotel is located close to mrt shandao temple station, bannan line. and also to taipei main station which is major starting spot of tour in taiwan.
But hotel facilities are a bit old and classic. hotel staffs are a bit amateur, not that professional, somewhat rude and unfriendly.
So overally, i dont recommend the hotel in consideration of price, facilities and staff attitude.
And one more, because i think many events are happening in the hotel, so many people were crowded in the lobby level. it was not comfortable atmosphere.
Male staff at counter is obnoxiously rude. Blame the delay with check-in on our group being too big. Else, rooms are large and very clean. Excellence view

Definitely not a 5 star hotel... more like 3 stars. The lobby is very dated with a 3-person sofa. The rooms are alright. Location is OK if you are willing to take busses, otherwise you may have to walk a bit to get to MRT station. The reception desk lacks customer service and often times abit unfriendly.
Service at the checking counter was very unfriendly.
bad service, the people on the reception.. they don't know how to deal with the customers.. they are rude ..don't waste your time on this hotel

Great place, clean, and everything.
Check-in counter staff is absolutely deplorable I have never encountered such ill-mannered staff. 
Full annoyed face and sharp words, didn't make an effort to confirm our requests, and failed to make simple confirmations. 
More so one of the staff completely ignored us and went past us directly beckoning her clients into the elevator. Afterwards the audacity of closing the elevator ON US who are waiting to enter the elevator. She swiped the card on the respective floors then AGAIN ignored us and left, fending us for ourselves.

Its a real shame the hotel would hire such unprofessional rookies as their front because all the other staffs were extremely warm and welcome.

The location was fantastic - just above taipei main station (via exit M6) through Caesar mall. Hotel is quite rundown - but it’s the longest standing hotel so it’s understandable. The keycard wasn’t the tap function but the insert function, and some lifts were very sensitive to the keycard too. Appreciate the service staff for their hospitality, although one of the service staff (a more mature counter lady) was quite rude and unhelpful. Don’t expect too much from the gym, amenities were old and on the brink of spoiling. 

But overall, good stay. Although it could be better in upkeep in the amenities.

Great location next to the train station. The staff on reception were very efficient and the hotel has a good gym. I didn’t like that they called my room to “remind me to check out”, which seems rude and not typical in hotels. Otherwise everything was fine.

The worst hotel experience I have ever encountered from their reception staff ! attitude just so rude. 
And the mattress is so soft that can sink to the floor.. 
not recommended.

The hardware is very good. Maybe it was because we were there during the Chinese New Year and there was no priority for guests to book the hotel's restaurant. I tried contacting the front desk: there was a lady named Tina who was unfriendly and unhelpful. She liked to taunt you very much. You know what she said. . . She alone can increase the hotel's rating. On the contrary, the concierge was very helpful and polite, and always responded to us in a timely manner. Overall evaluation: The hotel hardware is good and clean. The room service is very good. I give it 5 stars. But please don’t go to Taipei during the Spring Festival. We couldn’t book the hotel restaurant several weeks in advance. We were very unhappy and gave it 2 stars (Ctrip did not remind us that the hotel will not give priority to our stay). Guests book restaurants), the front desk has 2 stars, and the concierge has 5 stars!
The lady chef cooking at the egg station was so unfriendly it left a bad taste.

The service from the hotel front desk staff is not good. And they don’t respect the guests very much
I booked a birthday cake in advance, and the front desk told me on the day I picked it up that the hotel would arrange small cakes for guests. The next day they said they only had noodles. Then I made a reservation at the cake shop in the lobby, and the waiter immediately said, you need to pay yourself. Impolite attitude

The hotel is a big hotel brand, the room environment is OK, but the front desk is very unhelpful, and the check in and check out are understaffed. It took a long time to handle previous customers, and the courtesy is not good. Except for 101 Breeze Plaza, there are no other ********* places in this area. I will not choose this hotel or a hotel in this area next time.

The room is large, clean and located outside the Ximending business district. We were arranged to stay in the administrative building on the 2nd floor, but the window faced the exterior wall of another nearby building. There was no view at all and it felt quite oppressive.
The hotel breakfast tastes OK. It is on the 12th floor with a great view. However, the service of the waiter needs to be improved. There were some uneaten bread and coffee on the table. When I was about to go out to get other food, the waiter didn't pay any attention. In just a few seconds, he cleared the food that I hadn't enjoyed at all and put it on the table for other guests to use. This was not only a bit rude to the guests, but also a bit of a waste of food. The work awareness of the restaurant waiters needs to be strengthened.

I love our stay here at Taipei garden hotel. We brought my 82 yo mom and she was comfortable with the stay. Except for a rude front desk staff I encountered on an early morning time, our stay was perfect.

The female receptionist at the hotel was extremely rude. She kept interrupting the guest before they even finished speaking and kept talking about what she wanted to say. Besides being rude, she was also inattentive and unprofessional. She gave me the wrong room card and let me into someone else's room.

The location was very convenient. The staff were cheerful and friendly. There was only one staff member who spoke Japanese when we were there, so we couldn't communicate in broken English, and the staff who spoke Japanese didn't communicate very well. The breakfast was very delicious, and a seasoned traveler said that the breakfast at the Regent was better than any other hotel in the Taipei area. The women were also free to use the sauna and large communal baths attached to the pool and gym, so it was comfortable. There were no amenities such as body soap or shampoo in the men's room, which was a bit unfriendly. It was strange, but the bathroom in the room was comfortable. I was very glad that I was able to book a large room at a lower price than anywhere else on trip.com.

I've stayed at this hotel a few times before, primarily drawn by its excellent location and convenient transport links. However, after this most recent stay, I've decided I won't be choosing this hotel again.

The location is indeed superb; it's right outside Taipei Main Station, making it incredibly convenient even on a rainy day. Beyond the location, there's really not much else to commend it.

- The breakfast, costing over 100 RMB (roughly $15 USD), offers a limited selection, but it's adequate to fill you up.
- While the rooms appear to be cleaned and maintained to the best of their ability, they are old and dated. The air conditioning was ineffective, and a noticeable musty smell greets you upon entry.
- Check-in: Early check-in was unavailable, and we had to wait until after 3 PM. The front desk staff weren't rude, but they offered little in terms of assistance.
- The hotel frequently hosts large tour groups, especially from Japan and Korea, along with many families. Our neighboring rooms were occupied by other families, who were quite noisy, chatting loudly late into the night.

Personally, if you're solely prioritizing location, a short stay might be acceptable. However, for a relaxing family trip, I'd strongly advise choosing a newer hotel for a much-improved environment.

I checked the reviews earlier and some of them mentioned of bad service , rude receptionist however my encounters with the staff were good. I booked the triple room (smart AI room) with window and it was spacious and clean. Had a good selection of tv programs.  Location was good - opposite 24h carrefour supermarket, 10 mins walk to ximending and about 3-5 mins walk to mrt station And bus stop. The hotel is generally centrally location so even if you take a cab around it’s so convenient and inexpensive.  I definitely would stay there again with my family.  Shout out to Mr Harry (reception) for helping me with my reservation issues at 3am!

Excellent location, very convenient connect to MRT, bus, and taxi. However traffic around is always James. 
Cleaning crew is very good. 
Breakfast buffet is very limited. 
Front desk staffs are varied, some are pretty rude towards customers.

The bathrobes have changed from thick terry cloth to thin ones. The bath salts used to be a system where you could put in as much as you wanted, but now they are individually packaged. The ballpoint pens in the rooms have changed from the good knock-type ones to sustainable pencil-like ones. I'm sure some things have changed because of rude customers, but I have no complaints. It was Christmas time, so there was a big, beautiful tree and Santa made an appearance as part of an event. I asked if I could take a photo with him, but he said it was a paid thing. I wish he'd stop doing that because it was disappointing. Other than that, the hospitality was excellent and it's still the best hotel. Above all, everyone is kind. I want to use it again and again.

The hotel staff is highly unhelpful and with poor English, cannot offer help on the restaurant reservations and other requests. It is rather disappointed for a 5 stars hotel with such poor staff training…….
Very Grand with a lot of history  ! Room & Terrace & Bathroom were Awesome to Include our view ! Taipei people were very rude !

The front desk had a bad attitude when I checked in. When I asked questions, I was told not to ask them yet, but to wait until she finished her work before asking. Then she kept looking at the computer screen while talking, which was a bit disrespectful.

In addition, the hotel seems to be very close to Taipei MRT Station. In fact, it takes almost 15 minutes to walk there via the mall by taking the MRT Blue Line.

The room does not provide bottled water. You need to go to another room to fill it. If you live in a room at the end of the corridor, it is inconvenient. There is only one bottle for two people, and you have to fill it up almost four to five times a night.

Lobby staffs are excellent and helpful.  Breakfast are  standard asian cuisine. Exceptionally, the odd staff kept interfering while having breakfast.  Kept asking our group are taking advantage of breakfast as uninvited guests. Really very unprofessional. Really very unprofessional.

Realized that the night shift staff were unfriendly and a bit rude when I was there to collect my item in the morning. ☹️
Other than this, everything is ok and the housekeeping were helpful.  My husband and my daughter like the hotel room. Thks.

Not worth the price I pay for at all ,at Taipei Taiwan , to me just a 2.5 star local chain hotel , dint even achieved an international hotel  customer service standard at all , as I am also working in international hotel chain , I find it .. noting to shout about .. I find it ridiculous .. check in at 2.40pm  & receive check out call  at 11.07am … what a wired .. although we plan to check out at 11.15am … guys …  me & my family just not enjoying staying  in the hotel , lastly local guest itself  are rude ,  I can clearly understand that what the guest talking bad about ours as family tour guest in the local hotel , 😞, not enjoy not enjoy , not happy , sad , sad ,sad

for the price we paid the room is small. the receptionist is rude for a 5 star hotel. they cannot explain in a polite manner answers back rudely. i dont feel like i've entered a 5 star hotel.  Very far from xi men ding night market not convenient to walk around at night. room is small for the price we paid. in fairness the hotel is clean. but it's not worth the price we paid... we can get a better room for the price we paid.

location is a plus , side by side to TEINEX , 5 minutes walk. Rooms are comfy and clean. Also, a good shopping mall next door. Problem starts with food, specially at night. Unless you are a VIP , it is almost impossible to have lunch or dinner in their buffet. Lounge bar or room services are the only way to get some food in the hotel. Hostess at the buffet restaurant , very rude , always says ; ALL FULL ! Rooms service delivers dishes far from what the menu says , unless it is something really simple like a burger. Options are very few. Lounge bar offers basically the same menu as room service, but there you can make things right. Anyway, I would think twice before a book this hotel again.

Hotel location is very inconvenient and there's only 1 staff at the counter on the phone with no one else checkin us in. There's no swimming facilities and the staff at the Thai snacks is very impolite. Hotel room water was gushing out of the ceiling walls in the middle of the night and we had to change room. It is not a very old hotel and my first time encountering such bad service and stay from a 5 star hotel. This is the worse ever hotel and not worth a cent in my opinion.

The only good thing I can say about this hotel is its location is quite nice. Amenities are severely outdated. The entire hotel feels like a relic of the 1980s. It’s scheduled for a massive renovation and will probably be much better once they complete it. The front desk staff were extremely rude and unprofessional. I paid the deposit through trip.com then was required to pay again at the front desk upon checking in. When I went to check out they claimed that I had not paid anything at all. I even showed them the charges on my credit card and the trip.com transaction information. They only acquiesced when I threatened to call the police. I think this hotel is dealing with financial issues and is perhaps scamming unsuspecting guests.

The hotel has definitely the best location but the worst display of Taiwan in its staff. The staff was pretty rude, impatient and not willing to help. It just seems that they know they’ve got the best location so they can treat the guest however they want. As a Taiwan living abroad, I feel ashamed of being associated with these staff. The hotel should seriously retrain them better to better represent Taiwan.

The room is excellent but the buffet breakfast was not as good as expected.  Food choices are limited and no refill despite still have over 15 mins left before the end time.  There was absolutely no pork and tofu left in the sukiyaki pot.  Food were taken away before 10am.  Then, at 10am SHARP, the staff shut the curtain of the food area even the hot water bottle!  The staff were like asking us to leave as soon as possible after 10am.  I know they are just strictly following the time frame but it sounded really a bit rude.  
Other than that, staff at reception and entrance are good with courtesy.
Reception are rude.

Fat receptionist was either rude or she doesn’t understand my english. She kept on insisting i got an upgrade sent me to a king deluxe room which is old and creepy. I asked to change room, to a more modern room.
 I booked for a king deluxe
Not worth every penny i spent

📍The 3-person room is spacious, with room for 3 luggage. The bathroom has separate wet and dry areas and is clean.
📍The soundproofing is average.
📍The lobby is a bit dated.
📍The hotel staff are mostly female, with only 2-3 male staff members, who are generally unfriendly and reluctant to answer questions.
📍The hotel offers happy hour and a candy-filled event. 👍🏻
📍The hotel is close to the MRT station and a large 24-hour supermarket.
📍The airport bus stops across from the hotel, which is very convenient.

Location is excellent, being one of the few 4-star hotels linked to Taipei Main station. But it is China owned, and that is reflected in the distasteful deco of trying to look European and classy. Very dark in the hotel and room. The toilet design is bad, it is located next to the door with a circular bath tub and just plastic shower curtain. Staff performance is mixed, as I encountered a couple of rude and smileless mainland China staff as well as the helpful, friendly Taiwanese ones. I will look for another 4-star hotel nearby in my next trip.

5/23 morning 9:46 there is no any staff  at front desk. So many people are asking and waiting. Phone call is keep ringing and nobody show up and nobody answer.  We are in hurry and would like to ask to put luggage but no one is helping us. 
Very unprofessional staff. How come nobody stay at front desk. Many people are annoying. 

5/23 afternoon 3:30  I am going to pick up my luggage. No body staying at front desk again. So annoying. Many group are waiting. Very unprofessional staff.
Hotel has become just a mass transite for cheap bus tours. Staff are rude.

We went here for birthday celebration , the staff kindly prepared us a birthday cake for free (fyi: if ask for room decoration , need extra fee which I think was a bit overpriced ) however the staff were not helpful and kind at all. This is an eco-friendly hotel, thus no toothbrush and toothpaste would be provided which we didn’t know , when we asked the staff if they would provide it for us, he told us that “we suppose to bring our own stuff’’ in a rude manner and bad attitude ?? which I hv NEVER received such kind of “kindly advice’’ at any single “eco-friendly” hotel before. At last , they still sent us the toothpaste and toothbrush tho the experience was bad. Moreover the entire environment and room were soooooo dark and gloomy that make us feel so unpeaceful and inharmonious. There was water dripping sound all night long making us couldn’t sleep well. And at last we got sick and fever. To conclude highly NOT recommended this hotel for stay.

I recently stayed at the Miramar Hotel in Taipei and was quite disappointed with my experience. Despite being advertised as a 5-star hotel, it fell short in several areas.

Firstly, there were no complimentary water bottles, fruit, or any other welcome amenities in the room. This was quite surprising and not what I would expect from a hotel of this caliber.

The room itself was spacious, and got high floor room as requested, but it felt old and had a musty smell, which made the stay uncomfortable. Additionally, the bar in the hotel closed early, and there was no entertainment nearby, making the evenings quite dull.

To top it off, I missed breakfast one morning, and the staff was extremely rude, refusing to offer even a cup of coffee or orange juice. This lack of hospitality was very disappointing.

Overall, the facilities and service at Miramar Hotel did not meet the standards of a 5-star hotel. I would not recommend staying here.

Booked two rooms. Both came with river views. Rooms were clean and comfortable. Enough space for all of us to put our luggage and still move. However, the location is too far away from the train station. It is a long walk and that stretch is
rather quiet. 

Reception counter staff can be more friendly. When I asked for the key to another room I booked on the second night, the counter staff was curt and dismissive. It was already night time and we were tired. To have to put up with the attitude took some amount of patience. Not exactly one hotel I would make the effort to walk the distance the next time I stay at that area.

1. Misleading Entrance Signage
Upon arrival, we followed the signage pasted on a pillar that directed guests to a staircase entrance. However, when we reached that entrance, we were shocked to find the door marked with the sign “来宾止步” (“Guests Stop Here”). When we raised this with your staff, we were told that this entrance has not been in use since the COVID-19 period. While we understand that certain operations may have changed during the pandemic, COVID-19 restrictions have ended for more than two years. If the primary entrance has been permanently closed, why has no corrective action been taken and the misleading signage still left there? Carrying heavy luggage up and down a sloped path unnecessarily was frustrating and avoidable.
2. No Staff Assistance or Clear Signage at the New Entrance
When we finally located the new entrance, there were no staff members on standby to assist us, nor was there any clear external signage indicating that this was the correct way to access the lobby. The explanation given later was that all staff were away assisting with parking which is not acceptable. At least one person should have been assigned to remain at the entrance, or the last person leaving should have arranged for another colleague to cover the position. In addition, the Operations Director mentioned that there is signage inside the new entrance directing guests to take the elevator to the lobby. However, this logic is flawed. If guests cannot locate the correct entrance in the first place, how could they possibly see a sign placed inside?
3. Poorly Trained and Unprofessional Front Desk Behavior
After struggling outside, we called the number listed on Google. Only then did someone finally come out and lead us in. By that time, we were exhausted and upset. When we confronted the front desk staff about why they ignored us, despite us clearly visible outside the “来宾止步” glass door, making eye contact and knocking for help, but they claimed they “did not see us.” This excuse was clearly untrue, as we observed them looking in our direction. Even more disappointing, none of the front desk staff offered an apology even until we requested to speak to the Operations Director and asked him to review the CCTV footage. After reviewing the footage, the Operations Director confirmed that the front desk had not been alert and apologized on their behalf. However, he did not acknowledge that the front desk’s attitude and lack of sincerity were also serious problems. Being “not alert enough” and showing no sense of apology or empathy are two entirely different issues.

As an international hotel, the front desk is the first impression of your service. Regardless of the quality of your facilities, this poor experience completely overshadowed the positive aspects of our stay. It also severely damages the reputation of Kagaya Group — a brand that has long been admired for its exemplary Japanese hospitality and politeness. Although we appreciate the Operations Director’s effort to make amends by offering us a meal and gifts (which we declined), it remains undeniable that this incident reflects a failure in staff training and management oversight. 

We hope that management will seriously review this incident, especially the issues of:
- Inadequate and misleading signage at the entrance
- Lack of staff presence and assistance upon guest arrival
- Poor front desk awareness and unprofessional behavior
We trust that Kagaya Group will uphold its proud tradition of service by addressing these problems promptly and ensuring no other guests experience such treatment in the future.
Thank you for your attention.
All are good except location not very good. Room service staff quite impolite.  Shocked that Room deposit charged for 8000  money.
The toilet was smelly. The baggage handler was rude and made me sigh loudly.

Initially checked in a room at the end of the corridor and the entire corridor was messy with the Lancôme event, just felt unsafe with that environment and asked for a room move, was told that I had to be downgraded which I disagreed and asked for a room with same size, however I was moved to a room without bathtub, asked for room move again with bathtub and waited for 30 minutes in the room and the call center/ front desk kept unreachable, eventually we had to approach the Front Desk to get a new room key

There wasn’t even a simple apology, not talking about compensation, overall all staff are unfriendly, there’s almost no greeting at all at all areas

Very good, the room balcony is surprisingly large, clean and sanitary, much better than the windowless room I stayed in on the first day. You must have dinner at the Chinese restaurant in the lobby on the first floor (I forgot the name, it’s not a buffet). The chef's skills are first-rate, but the waiters are untrained. It's not that they are bad, but unprofessional. Since they charge a 10% service charge, they should be professional, especially when it comes to opening the wine. I ordered a bottle of red wine, and everything from opening the bottle to pouring the wine and the subsequent processes were all unsatisfactory, and they didn't even take the basic steps to open the wine. This really should be improved. A bottle of wine is more expensive than the meal. This kind of service is really substandard. I hope it can be improved.

This is my second time staying at the hotel within the same year. Stayed with my family and friends this time round. 

Plus points: Rooms are spacious, Excellent view, Prompt service. Good spread of breakfast. Top floor gym offering almost panoramic view of surroundings.

Area that can be improved:
The housekeeping of the hotel rooms can be further improved. Despite the rooms that we were staying in have been recently renovated (why are there 2 letters indicating renovating that almost span 1 year), the general cleanliness of the room is much to be desired and definitely can be improved. One of the rooms that we were staying have to be cleaned again before we stayed in (I'll spare the details here).  Was offered "compensation" in the form of drinks voucher. However, instructions for the drinks voucher at taipei garden hotel thai restaurant are not clear. It is indicated redemption is between 1400 to 1700 daily which we are usually not at the hotel within that timing. Service by the staff at the thai restaurant is also below par and borderline on being unfriendly.

Despite the above, special praise to the 打扫阿姨 thats on duty for 28th of August morning; bumped in to her during leaving the room. Left feedback of the areas of the room that's found to be unsatisfactory clean previously. She took the feedback given seriously and clean the room thoroughly when we were away. Excellent and detailed cleaning for service recovery,

I stayed for 4 nights and 5 days from March 10 to 13.
On the first day, I arrived at 1 PM and waited until 2 PM to check in and was assigned to the 1-bed room that I had requested in advance.
For reference, the female staff during the day felt a bit stiff.
I have been working in the service industry for over 15 years, but I felt like I needed some training on customer service.
On the other hand, the female staff who spoke Korean seemed to be running around trying to solve problems, but I was disappointed that she seemed to lack professionalism.
When I asked for a high floor at the front desk, they assigned me to the 11th floor, which was not bad.
The rooms were cleaned cleanly during the 4 nights and 5 days, and the bathroom was also cleaned well, so I was able to relieve my fatigue in the bathtub after every tour.
The only regret was that there were no cotton pads among the amenities.
Other than that, I think I was satisfied with everything.
Later, I heard that this hotel was visited by many Japanese people, so there were many people who were fluent in Japanese. I would rate this as one of the top five hotels I've ever stayed at in Asia.

The hotel lacks seating, causing long wait times for guests to check into their rooms and leaving visitors with nowhere to sit and chat! It would be perfect if there were a place near the lobby to have coffee and snacks sold at the entrance!

Generously sized rooms, ample breakfast selection. Very helpful staff.  I would definitely stay again. ￼ The only negative that I did notice was that they really do make everyone wait until 3 PM to check in.

Front counter staff, Ms Whale is very helpful.   She has recommended us to go for coffee at Louisa Coffee and to explore the Daan Forest park while waiting to check-in.    
Hotel location is strategically located about 5 min walk from Daan Park station.   
There is a beef noodles stall nearby the hotel that is so delicious and affordable.  I’m sure it taste better than the famous Yong Kang Beef noodles.  
Thank you for the wonder stay.  Appreciate it.

台北車站 has become an old district this decade. Caesar Hotel displayed this image completely: old. Carpet has blood stain. Check-in was delayed. Attitude of counter servicers are differentiably worser than Taichung's. The family mart underneath will closed. Better options are available with this price. It is also understandable the reason of the star-rating lowering from 5 to 4.

We ended up at the Hilton Taipei Xinyi on Songgao Road due to a booking error, and it happened to be the 228 holiday, so the price was high. The room was smaller than we expected. Taipei seems to have a frugal approach, as there were too few housekeeping staff, making room cleaning very slow, and we had to wait several hours to check in. The hotel lobby is small and separate from the front desk, which is located on the 6th floor. Compared to hotels of the same caliber in mainland China, there's a significant gap in terms of price, service quality, and speed. It's also quite far from Taoyuan Airport; a taxi ride costs around 1600 TWD, which is about 350 RMB.

A hotel I have stayed at many times for about 30 years.
I think it's in the best location for Japanese people.
This stay was for 2 consecutive nights.

Bad points
1. Since I arrived in Taipei early in the morning, I only left my suitcases and other luggage. Just to be safe, I told the front desk that I had booked two consecutive nights starting today. When I asked about the check-in time, etc. It starts at 3pm, so please come after that. Your luggage will be kept in the cloakroom, so please go there."
First of all, here, I slightly deduct points for hospitality.

2. Next, I returned to the hotel to check in around 3:30pm.
Facing the entrance, the check-in counter was on the right and the concierge desk was on the left, but since this was my first stay since before the coronavirus, I couldn't tell which was the check-in counter.
There were hotel staff all over the place, but guests were lining up in the same way with similar desks, and I didn't know which way to check in. In the end, I had to ask the hotel staff. .
I thought this was a star-rated hotel where if there were any anxious customers who were lost, the hotel staff would be able to spot them and call out to them, but it seems that was not the case.
I ended up having to go to the counter myself and ask where I should line up to check in.

3. After checking in, I got off the elevator on my way to my room, walked down the hallway, and suddenly looked down to see that the bottom of the wallpaper in the hallway had peeled off the glue and was peeling off.
Wasn't this a 5 star hotel? I can understand if it's 3 stars, but...

4. It was hot in the room at sunrise on the second day, so I checked the air conditioner and found that it wasn't blowing enough cool air to relieve the heat and was broken.
When I contacted the front desk, they came to check and told me that it was indeed broken and that they would lend me a circulator, so please take care of it.
Wasn't this a 5 star hotel? I can understand 2 stars, but...
Naturally, I requested a room change on the spot.
Fortunately, there seemed to be a vacant room, so I was able to change the room, but I didn't want it to be a downgrade, so I checked and was told it was an upgrade.
As a result, it was true that the 12th to 14th floors (there is no 13th floor) were the upper floors, but the rooms were actually smaller. Is this an upgrade? ? ?

5. I always looked forward to the breakfast here, but the standard has clearly gone down.
Everything provided is the same for both nights.
The quality of the content has also deteriorated compared to before.
I always order an omelet that is made on the spot at any hotel, as is the case with most of the offerings.
I ordered it again this time, but it wasn't a fluffy, fluffy omelet, but rather a baked roll with ingredients.

Good point
After waiting for a while at check-in, the young front desk man was very nice and told me that he had an upgraded room for me.
(As a result, I changed rooms on the second day, so I ended up returning to the original grade room???)

As a hotel that has been in business for over 30 years, there may be noticeable imperfections here and there, but if it is to claim to be one of the best five-star hotels in Taipei, it may have to improve its facilities, food, and hospitality.
My good impression of Regent Taipei has disappeared this time.
Next time I'll be staying in Taipei, I'll probably stay in Okura, even if it's a little more expensive.

The hotel itself is quite good but the service was not up to standard at all. We were waiting for quite a while for check-in even it was 6pm. Both counters were serving people booking a room on-spot which took a long time to complete. There were empty counters but no staffs had any intention to open them and serve the long queue. 
We ended up waiting a lot longer than we should. And I did not expect that to happen in a hotel like this. When we were served finally, it only took us less than 3 minutes to get the keys and settled everything since we booked the room in advance. 

The stay was fine but something weird happened after we check-out. I got an email from the hotel saying that I left some skincare products in the room and they asked me whether I need to get that back. 
However, I did not recall leaving anything behind. I politely asked them to take a picture and send it to me to confirm whether that was mine. But I never got any reply. 
I think they made a mistake with the room number and contact me by mistake. But the least they can do is to write back to me instead of ghosting me completely. What kind of customer service is that? Definitely appalling.

When you check in, you still have to wait for the room to be cleaned. There is a drink at the bar to take a rest, but it's a bit exaggerated to have to wait since you didn't check in very early. The room is clean, the bed and pillows are hard, and the swimming pool is beautiful

Stayed for 2 nights in total. The outdoor swimming pool has a good temperature. The gym room is 3-pointed but it's decent. There are also staff who frequently disinfect.
The bathtub is also big and soaking in the bath is comfortable
The Christmas decorations are in place and check-in is a bit slow.

Old facilities but acceptable
Staff service attitude is good
The only downside is that there is only one washing machine and one dryer, and there are often long queues
The gym room opens very early, and the hotel is directly connected to the underground shopping mall and MRT, which is very convenient

The check-in time is very slow, there is no service, the hygiene is poor, no one cleans the room every day, and no one comes unless you call to clean it. When we checked in, we agreed to a late check-out, but they said we hadn't said that and even told us to call the police. It's a really rubbish hotel. Don't come, don't stay at this hotel. We booked two rooms and 4 little babies, but they urged us to check out immediately in the morning, and the door card was also blocked. They said they would call the police. It's a rubbish hotel.

Strategic location, close to MRT and many restaurants nearby. Service is a bit poor because I had to wait a long time to check in. The noise outside the room is so loud that I had trouble sleeping. Old hotel but good facilities. Thankyou..

1. We arrived hotel at 2pm but the staff said must wait until 3 pm only can check in. This is hotel policy. 2. Hotel lobby not provide seat for customer. Lobby only have counter check in and open space to storage luggage. 3. The room not spacious coz they add in extra bed become triple room. Actually the room space is for twin bed room. So quite terrible for us to handle our luggage everyday.

The environment is beautiful, the transportation is convenient, the parking lane is spacious, and it is worthy of being a five-star chain hotel. The only drawback is that the counter is too small, and you need to wait for some time to check in. Everything else is perfect￼

It was a surprise to me that a 5 star hotel does not provide toiletries like tooth brush and hand soap, the most basic thing. Although the reason is for environmental friendliness, I guess, hand wash liquid or soap is the basic necessities  and for hygiene purpose.  Not all guests will use the toothbrush but as a 5 star hotel, at least those who really in need can request from the hotel. Instead, guests are required to purchase, as stated in the terms. 
Cleanliness and staff are great though.  Near to MRT station too and some eateries.  Check in is slow, not sure if the staff is new or the system is not good.

This time I was going to the Taipei Arena to attend a concert, so I booked a hotel close to the Taipei Arena. From Taipei Main Station, take the Bannan Line to Zhongxiao Fuxing Station, Exit 2, turn right and walk straight for about 5 minutes. It is also very close. Howard Plaza is a hotel with a long history, but it does not feel old. The only drawback is that we had to wait very long to check in. Because we checked in 10 minutes early, we queued up here once. As the room was not ready yet, we were told that we had to wait until 3 o'clock to get the room card. They gave us a sign, and then at 3 o'clock, we were queued in the queue for room cards early. There were only 5 people in front of me, and by the time I was checked in, I had used up more than 40 minutes (the other team checked in after 3 o'clock and was very fast). After getting the room card with great difficulty, there was no strange smell when entering the room. The bed and toilet were very clean, but the bed and pillow were too soft. Friends who like to sleep on hard pillows should consider this. The toilet had a bidet and was very clean. The water from the shower head was very good, not hot or cold, and it was very comfortable to take a bath. There was a bathtub for bathing. My son said that the water would become less and less as time went by. I laughed and thought it might be because the plug didn't fit properly. I'm not used to taking a bath outside, so this didn't make much difference. The other indoor slippers are thicker than those in other hotels, but they will feel stuffy after wearing for a long time. People who easily sweat on their feet should pay attention. This is my daughter’s experience. There are many breakfast items, but the taste needs to be improved. I personally think the best thing is the simplest porridge with some side dishes. The accommodation is good overall and comfortable. I will consider choosing Fuhua again next time.

Our check-in was delayed, and even after asking several times, the staff didn’t apologize—instead, they just kept saying they were handling it. We had to ask on our own if we could check out late to get any kind of compensation for the delay.

Our flight was canceled, so check-in was delayed until the next day, but they responded sincerely to my email in Japanese.
Thank you for upgrading our room as well.
I was very happy after all the bad luck we've had.
Hotel check-in is very slow and needs improvement
Waiting time for check in was too long, nearly take abt 1 hr!!

Clean . comfy bed and pillow .  Staff is friendly and helpful. However the reception a bit slow for registration due to 1 man power available, wait for 15 min for check in process which is out of my expectation.  15 min walking distance to XinMenDing . There also shutter available from the hotel ,do book in advance if you need the service.  Lots of Singaporean stay in this hotel . So it good to stay .

It's located right next to the station, so it's very easy to move around with a suitcase.
The dim sum restaurant on the second floor is also delicious.
However, the hotel entrance and area around the check-in counter are quite busy. I think it would be perfect if it was a little more quiet to wait for check-in.

Paid a premium to stay in this hotel during their peak period. The price was almost doubled.  During check-in, they have only 2 counters to serve the normal guests which we have to wait rather long.  Check-in was quite slow.  The rooms size are huge especially the bath room.  This is the first time I encountered a hotel did not check to ensure that the towels they provide to their guests must be clean and unused.  The towel in my room has weird stain on it that really look so disgusting (not sure what was it). It really freak me out when I almost use it!  After my complain, they changed new towels for me and offered some free In-room service to compensate.

The service is good. There are still many tourists when you check in on weekdays. You have to wait a while to check in. There are many breakfast options, but they are all ordinary. There are no amazing meals. The bar is very ordinary, but the room facilities are well maintained.
Check in very slow, wait over 30 mins.

In terms of location, the hotel is located next to Taipei Main Station. There are also large shopping malls and underground shopping malls nearby, which is quite convenient. However, the way back to the hotel from the train/MRT is not easy to identify, and the underground streets are always complicated.

Basically, this time I checked in mainly for Junpin's famous buffet breakfast. The dishes are very rich. In addition to the food and drink selections from famous ********* stores, there is also a self-service beef shabu-shabu option. You can also scan the QR code on the counter. Food is prepared right away, no need to wait in long queues. In addition, there are also cold noodles, common cooked food and cold cuts, desserts and ice cream, all in all you will be very full. However, when I told my room number when I arrived at the restaurant, the staff questioned me that I had already had breakfast, but I had just woken up. This was puzzling. Maybe issuing meal coupons directly would avoid the problem of someone stealing breakfast?

I knew before departure that the hotel would not provide "disposable supplies", but I still hope that the hotel could clarify in advance that those "disposable supplies" would not be provided, and would provide sterilized slippers to facilitate travelers to prepare necessary disposable supplies in advance. spare parts.

In addition, I arrived at the hotel at about 18:00, and there was only one person in charge of checking in. However, there were several groups of people waiting to check in. The check-in efficiency was a little slow, and it took about 10 minutes for a second staff member to help check in. The strain is relatively poor.

There is an ice water/cold water/sparkling water machine on the room floor, which is convenient for environmental protection and can also cool down the heat. However, the height of the hot water kettle is not convenient for the washbasin in the room. To make hot water, you have to fill the water machine with the water machine. At the same time, the hot water kettle is unknown. It "automatically drains water from the bottom" every once in a while, which is really strange. There is sufficient air conditioning in the room, but the circular bathtub is located next to the door. Even if you can hear the conversation in the corridor, you can't fully soak in it.

The staff was very attentive. On our first check-in, a Cantonese-speaking waiter was assigned to assist us with check-in procedures and provide a detailed explanation of the various amenities. The breakfast was rich and exquisite, and I especially recommend the ********* breakfast, which comes with a generous serving of fruit. The braised pork rice was excellent, not too salty or greasy, yet with a traditional flavor. While the bar offers a wide selection of complimentary dishes, I particularly enjoyed the three Chinese teas. Xinjin quenches my thirst, and sitting on a small sofa, gazing at the lush green mountain views from the sixth floor, the only sounds of Zen are truly a delight. The location is close to the Museum of Chinese Art, so if you arrive early, you can visit there while waiting to check in. The shuttle bus was also elegant and clean, and the driver was friendly. Overall, it was a clean, quiet, and elegant place to rest.

One suggestion for improvement: We stayed two nights and had breakfast both days. After breakfast on the first day, we explained our special requests for the second day's breakfast, asking what to leave out or what to add. It would have been great if they could have accommodated us on the second day. Also, if the waiter could speak ********* Mandarin a little slower, it would have made communication easier for Hong Kong residents who speak a little Mandarin. If the bar switches from cola to rice tea or detoxifying herbal tea, it will be more consistent with the overall health style.

Transportation and eating are convenient, directly connected to the subway exit, opposite the Starlight March Shopping Center, surrounded by many snacks, milk tea and convenience stores. The room is quite spacious by Taipei standards, the hygiene is good, and the towels and bathrobes are very clean. The facilities have a sense of age, the quality of the shampoo provided is not good, and the hair is frizzy after washing. Not even moisturizer/hand cream provided. There are many guests and the lobby downstairs is busy. You need to wait for check-in and you cannot delay check-out.

Location: the hotel is located near to Taipei Main Station (exit M3). Convenient to move around the area. There are shopping malls and eateries nearby eg Tim Ho Wan. U can also walk to Ningxia Night Market (about 25-30mins walk)
Cleanliness: Hotel is clean and poshed!
Amenities: I love the hair conditioner! Disposable slippers, razor, facial cottons/buds, toothbrushes are provided.
Service: excellent. They offer us a complimentary drink each when the check-in was delayed. Staff are helpful and polite. 
Food: We did not eat the hotel breakfast as we love the local dishes. There are many eateries nearby at main station. There is also a family mart next door. The oat latte in the cafe, located at the hotel’s entrance,  is aromatic and nice.

Pros: 1. Connected directly to Taipei Station. Literally centre of Taipei city 2. Reasonable room size Cons: 1. No blackout curtain in the room. You will be waken up by daylight. 2. Long queue for check-out.
Check in too slow,I booked 2 room but take 2.5hrs to get second room

Excellent

Elegant environment, considerate service, small cups of ice cream and tea served waiting for check-in.
There are welcome fruits, provide aerated healthy clean water, lotion, courteous enough.
The room is designed in British style, with a large desk, which is unique and noble.
Bath salt is provided next to the bathtub, which is located between the door and the bath children, which is very special and convenient for children to play in the water.
The breakfast buffet is served with exquisite desserts and natural ingredients, as well as Movenpick ice cream/bar all-you-can-eat, lemon syrup and dark chocolate.
Just downstairs is a large trendy shopping mall, transfer station and Taipei Station, with a superior location.
There is a door gate between the room and the toilet, which allows them to communicate with each other and facilitate communication


bad

There is a large square between the bathroom and the bathtub, standing bathing when there is a cool breeze from the room pumped in, the design can be optimized, if there is an overhead shower better, hot water in two twists to control the water temperature is more inconvenient.
The much-anticipated buffet breakfast is like going to the British royal family to enjoy, the variety is exquisite, but can strengthen the food characteristics of different countries, such as providing ********* authentic cuisine: taro ball, fried chicken steak, ********* bubble milk tea and so on.

We stayed on the 10th floor and had a beautiful city view, just as I had requested through Agoda. The hotel staff were incredibly accommodating and prepared everything as requested, which made our stay even more special.

Room:
The room was spacious enough for the four of us, including an infant. It felt cozy, was well-lit, and offered a lovely view. The beds were extremely comfortable, and the hallways were clean and nicely designed.

Cleanliness:
Even though we left our room untidy after heading out each day, the housekeeping staff did an impressive job of tidying everything up.

Internet:
The Wi-Fi was fast, which allowed me to work seamlessly at night.

Breakfast:
The breakfast was delicious, though there was a long queue depending on the time we went. We loved the wide variety of food options available.

Staff:
The staff were attentive and efficient. Whenever I requested items, they delivered them to our room in less than 10 minutes (though I assume this may vary depending on the time of day). It was my birthday during our stay, and they left a thoughtful letter and they even sent a small but delicious cake to celebrate the occasion.

Perks:
One fun perk was that they provided us with two plastic bags, which we could fill with complimentary candies and chocolates everyday.

Location:
The hotel is conveniently located just a 15-minute walk from Ximending Night Market. We also used their shuttle bus service to visit Longshan Temple.

Overall:
Our trip to Taipei was fantastic, and this hotel contributed to the experience. I would definitely recommend it to others and would love to stay here again.

I was disappointed in Taipei Garden. The location is excellent. However, check-in was slow and unorganized. We arrived at 3pm, the check in time, to long lines and our rooms not being ready. Then, the staff wrote down the wrong room number and my 80-year old parents had to go up and down and wait over 20-min before it could be resolved and they were let into their room. 

The hotel lobby does not have a true “lobby” sitting area where guests could meet us. Decor also was a bit kitschy. Overall, it was a disappointment compared to other 5-star hotels we stayed in in Taiwan and Taipei.

I think this is a 2 star old hotel. There is nothing good about it except that it is close to the station. The check-in process is very slow. For breakfast, there are many empty seats, but I waited for ten minutes, and there were more than ten people in line. But there were dozens of empty seats inside.

The location is great if you plan to visit Taipei Dome and nearby areas, but otherwise my stay at this hotel was unpleasant.

My room wasn’t ready at check-in, which delayed my schedule. I was offered late checkout until 1 PM, but the hotel called me at 12:30, woke me up, and rushed me to check out.

The room’s Wi-Fi and TV didn’t work. I didn’t want to deal with it at night, so I just connected to the Wi-Fi from the room next door.

You can also clearly hear people talking in the next room and loud water noises from the bathroom.

We arrived at 1:00 that day. We thought we would have to wait until 3:00 to check into the room. We wanted to leave our luggage there and go for a walk. Unexpectedly, they said that everything was ready and we could check in right away. It was great. When we walked in, we saw that the room was large and spacious. The sofa chair was very comfortable. We immediately curled up in the chair and read the detective novel we brought. The slippers were of good quality. There was someone to open the door when we entered or left. When we went upstairs, there was someone to help press the elevator or remind us which elevator was open. The service was very good. It was opposite the Taipei Arena and there were many places to eat nearby. It was really convenient. If I had to say anything bad, the bathtub was a bit high. It was a bit hard for people with short legs to step in or out of the bathtub. The breakfast price was a bit high, so I couldn't taste whether it was delicious. But I was still very satisfied.

The location might be far but there is free shuttle service. It’s just you might have to review the schedule to see it will fit your planning. If you plan to come back late, you might have to take taxi. And sometimes, at some peak hours, you might  not be able to get on the shuttle because of a long queue. Other than that, everything is perfect. The staff is so nice that is willing to help you send out postcards after their work hours.

The front desk asked me to wait until 3 pm to check in when I arrived earlier. After I came back at 3 pm, the front desk still told me the room was not ready, and she didn't know when it could be ready. After traveling the whole day and being unable to get a room upon arrival despite following their policy, and having to face the cold reaction of the front desk, it's disappointing.

I made a reservation online with the wrong date. I contacted the customer service center a minute later and asked to change the date. I was pushed back and forth by the platform and the hotel. I contacted the customer service center and waited for a long time, but still ignored it.

Large room, clean and comfortable.  Breakfast is excellent.
Check in process very slow need improvement.
This time, the wait time for check-in was long and the staff's attitude was cold. I don't want to use it next time.

At the huge Taipei Main Station, "Tiancheng University Arrival Store" can be easily reached by following the signs. Great location, easy to go everywhere. The hotel is a bit old, but overall it is not bad.

We had a windowless room. Good size room and bathroom; both were updated so it was comfortable. Staff and service were excellent, and the facilities were well maintained. Iconic views from all areas of the property. Highly recommended.

I've booked this place multiple times when I come to Taiwan. The surrounding transportation is convenient, and the downstairs restaurant is quite good. 

**Hygiene**: Clean and tidy, which is reassuring.

**Environment**: Beautiful and refreshing. I'll definitely recommend it to friends.

Hotel bersih dan selesa. Bilik air ada bidet dan tempat mengambil wudhu. Setiap hari boleh collect free complimentary biskut dan air minuman di cafe. The hotel is conveniently located close to the nearest station, making transportation easy and offering good value for money. The breakfast selection is not as extensive as a buffet, but the quantity was sufficient, and it was very delicious. The staff were kind, and even those who didn’t speak Japanese greeted us with smiles, which was nice.

Although the facilities are old since it is a long-established hotel, everything was cleaned well, so I was comfortable during my stay. I recommend it for those who enjoy retro experiences. 

After checking out, I stored my luggage and when I returned from sightseeing, I requested two taxis. The staff immediately went outside to hail a taxi for us and waved goodbye with smiles until the end. There were nine of us staying together, and everyone was satisfied. Some were visiting Taiwan for the first time, and it turned out to be a great trip. Thank you very much.
great location, great breakfast !
Although it is a little far from the downtown area, I think it is a good value hotel considering the breakfast options and the extensive facilities such as the sauna.

The hotel is new, the facilities are good, the breakfast is also rich, the service attitude is good, the location is very good, it is very suitable for business trips and travel accommodation, I will come again next time I go on a business trip, it is worth recommending

Highly recommended, worth repurchasing!

This is our first time in Taipei and this hotel was bonus for this trip. Centrally located to all tourist spots and major night markets.  Taxi and Uber to everywhere is very affordable. had a pleasant week staycation, i will definitely recommend it if you mainly take taxis to popular tourist destination. overall a great hotel right in the middle of taipei.
We booked an executive suite. The room was very clean and comfortable, and the service staff had a very good attitude👍. Will recommend friends to stay here.

The room is spacious and comfortable. I read many reviews saying the room is too dark. But it's not true. The room is well lit and super comfortable. Very cozy. I enjoyed my stay and highly recommend this hotel !
The hotel is located at a great location for easy transport around the city and to the airport.

Whenever I return to Taiwan, I always make sure to stay here for a few days. Although the hotel is a renovated old building, the rooms are quite comfortable and the hygiene is satisfactory. I definitely recommend it.
Great location and always helpful staff. Rooms are a bit outdated but clean and spacious enough.

I have stayed many times, and I have never been disappointed with the service level of Meifu and the experience provided to guests. In addition, the Italian restaurant on the fourth floor is highly recommended. The quality of steaks, other side dishes, and pastries is satisfactory.

The room is clean, hygienic and bright, and there is still room to move around after opening the two 28-inch luggage. Stayed for three nights and had a good experience. ￼

The accommodation fee is reasonable among 5 star hotel nearby.

Facility is old but the cleanness is acceptable.

Toilet is shower toilet, which is good for Japanese lol.

Here below is 2 nagative points.
1. number of outlets are very limited. no outlet nearby bedside, which is very inconvenience.
2. location is a bit far from stations. If it is rain, it may make you awkward to go outside.

This hotel has lots of rooms, so the lift may be crowded in certain time. It has some risk to make you irritated. Fortunately, I didn't have a such situation though.

Overall, this hotel can be recommended if the price can keep reasonable as seen this time.

A hotel with an excellent location. It is quiet at night and the surrounding environment is convenient~~ It feels like going home when you go back to the hotel at night. Parking is also convenient. The only fly in the ointment may be that you may not know where the check-in counter is when you come for the first time. We prepare birthday cake! ten out of ten 🫡🫡

The location and environment of the hotel are very good. It only takes about 10 minutes to walk from the Xinbeitou MRT.
The facilities in the hotel are very exquisite and beautiful, and the rooms are very spacious. The toilet and bathroom are separate, which feels good.
The service staff are kind and friendly, making guests feel at home.
Highly recommend to stay and will stay again.

Excellent location with a view of Taipei 101, and a shopping mall right downstairs!
